DT.01.additionalInfo: The reaction area of these points is related to secretion. These are important points in Master Tung's acupuncture for treating conditions involving toxicity in the body. The points can help secrete and expel toxins from the body. The points are treated with bloodletting. Some practitioners, who are not direct students of Master Tung, apply cupping to the area after bloodletting to help release more blood. However, Master Tung did not use cupping when bloodletting the back, chest, and abdomen. In these areas, the bloodletting is superficial. Master Tung preferred bloodletting over acupuncture to avoid damaging internal organs, so there is no need for a large amount of blood to be released after the procedure. The technique involves pinching the point with the thumb and index finger, followed by bloodletting. When we look at points DT.OI and DT.02, known as the Branch Separators, we are looking at something much bigger than just local points. They belong to a very special, almost secretive category in Master Tung's system called the '32 Relieving Points', or Jie Zhen. The Chinese character 'Jie' [ % is profound. It means to untie a knot, to melt, to release, or to eliminate. These points act as the body's emergency release valves. Master Tung actually kept this specific system quite hidden, revealing only about 18 of the 32 points. You might already know point 22.10, Shou Jie, which we use to instantly release needle shock or sharp pain. But DT.OI and DT.02 are your heavy hitters for toxicity. Look at the indications: snakebites, drug overdoses, food poisoning, toxic gas. These points are literal antidotes; they expel severe poisons from the blood. But you don't have to wait for a snakebite to use them. In the modern clinic, we use them for severe dermatological toxicity—like weeping eczema, intense allergic dermatitis, and pruritus. We also use them when internal toxic heat is trying to escape the body, manifesting as foul body odor or bad breath. By bleeding these points, you activate the 'Jie' function—you untie the pathology, release the trapped heat, and completely eliminate the toxicity from the bloodstream. These points can be used for patients who have undergone chemotherapy or radiation treatments to help the body expel the toxins accumulated from these therapies. DT.18.additionalInfo: The bloodletting regions for the internal organs on the back are located on the surface of the back, covering a broad area above the organ. There are five bloodletting regions for internal organs, which can be identified relative to the spinous processes. These areas overlap with the VT points. In each zone, bloodletting regions are found through palpation and visual examination. We check for hardening of the connective tissue via palpation, and visually search for Luo channels.
